nodes.rationale: Not used because it lacks safety comments around unsafe FFI calls and safer Windows FFI patterns exist.

nodes.label: Redbook
nodes.rationale: Glue crate that brings together CD audio crates into a coherent whole, plus Windows apps for ripping and tagging.

nodes.label: Create TOC and query online directories
nodes.norm_label: create toc and query online directories

nodes.label: Avoid nesting principle
nodes.rationale: Flat code is easier to reason about; nested code should be longer than it is wide.

nodes.label: Code ordering standards
nodes.rationale: Modules should read like a table of contents and functions like natural-language explanations.

nodes.label: Error handling standards
nodes.rationale: Prefer custom error types and ? propagation; avoid unwrap and expect in library code.

nodes.label: Nightly toolchain requirement
nodes.rationale: Formally documented in rust-toolchain.toml; enables experimental features for readability and ergonomic API design.

nodes.label: Readability standards
nodes.rationale: Leverage the type system, clear code ordering, and flat control flow so code reads like natural language.

nodes.label: Testing standards
nodes.rationale: Follow standard Rust conventions and focus tests on behavior rather than implementation.

nodes.label: Unsafe code policy
nodes.rationale: Unsafe code is limited to specific hardware access modules and must never be modified or created by agents.

nodes.label: Nightly-only toolchain policy
nodes.rationale: Needed to rely on downstream crates that use nightly features and to gain ergonomic benefits.

nodes.label: thread_safely::Context
nodes.rationale: Allows cancellation of long-running IO in multi-threaded applications.

nodes.label: Encode music
nodes.rationale: Encodes ripped music to WAV or FLAC.

nodes.label: Thread safety via separate traits
nodes.rationale: File handles are not Sync; separate AudioCdExt and AudioCdExtMut traits let users mutate metadata before locking and spawning threads.

nodes.label: Red Book/Album Cover Motif
nodes.rationale: The cover uses a deep red gradient (#e0343c to #a3141d) with dark spine shadow lines near the left edge, reading as both a hardcover book (the 'red book' pun) and a CD album case; the square bottom-right corner anchors it to the page strip.
nodes.source_location: cover path: M116 40 H60 Q40 40 40 60 V196 Q40 216 60 216 H216 V140 Z, fill url(#cover)

nodes.label: Compact Disc (Disc with Rainbow Sheen)
nodes.rationale: The disc is drawn with concentric guide rings, a hub hole matching the dark background color, and an iridescent linear-gradient sheen (blue-purple-pink-mint) to evoke a real polycarbonate CD surface, placing it behind and through the cut in the cover.
nodes.source_location: circles at cx=212 cy=52, fills url(#disc) and url(#sheen)

nodes.label: Embossed Music Note
nodes.rationale: A beamed double eighth note is embossed in the icon's dark background color (#12151b, 0.85 opacity) on the red cover, stating that the project is about music/audio content rather than data CDs.
nodes.source_location: g transform=translate(76 108) scale(1.9), two-ellipse beamed note

nodes.label: Redbook-rip App Icon (icon.svg)
nodes.rationale: App branding for the redbook-rip crate: the name references the 'Red Book' CD-DA (Compact Disc Digital Audio) standard, visualized as a literal red book cover with an embedded compact disc and music note, signaling that the project extracts audio CDs.

nodes.label: Diagonal Cut Composition
nodes.rationale: The cover's top-right corner is sliced off diagonally so the CD shows through the cut, a design decision that fuses the book and disc motifs into one silhouette and visually communicates 'extracting the disc from the album/book'.

nodes.label: Candidate release cover thumbnails (interactive release selection)
nodes.norm_label: candidate release cover thumbnails (interactive release selection)
nodes.rationale: The thumbs/ directory holds one cover-art thumbnail per candidate release (six files for the six Definitely Maybe pressings offered in release_selection.txt), so the ripper can show cover art to let the user visually distinguish between the multiple matched releases during interactive release selection.

nodes.label: definitely_maybe test fixture
nodes.rationale: The definitely_maybe asset directory models a ripped audio CD (11 .cda track stubs plus TOC.hex/CDROM_TOC.hex) together with a MusicBrainz disc-id lookup result (musicbrainz.json), release_selection.txt, and per-release-candidate cover-art thumbnails keyed by release MBID in thumbs/. It exists to exercise redbook's metadata lookup, release selection, and cover-art thumbnail handling against realistic data.

nodes.label: MusicBrainz Release 20c0689b-0f10-3d9e-9740-ed06fb39dd5c (Definitely Maybe, 2000 Jewel Case)
nodes.rationale: The thumbnail's filename is the MusicBrainz release MBID. musicbrainz.json lists this release as a 'Definitely Maybe' 2000 Jewel Case edition whose cover-art-archive has exactly one image (front=true, back=false, count=1), so the thumbnail is most plausibly that sole front cover image.
